## Purpose

Recover an explicitly identified historical task holder after failed publication
left legacy branch owners, terminal job pins or a READY task's stale assignment.
The source checkout remains available for operator salvage.

## When a playbook uses it

Live playbook invocation is gated. A local operator or live global supervisor
uses the CLI/API control after examining the historical task and session.

## How it works internally

The handler in `src/commands/retained_holder_repair.py` checks recorded task/session
provenance, provider stop confirmation, strict local process inventory, workspace
and owner fences, job identities, and Git repository contents. `apply: false`
previews that evidence and returns a digest. Apply must present that exact digest
and repeats the proofs after preserving Git work and locking the database rows.

## Side effects and persistence

Apply creates immutable local Git refs for HEAD, index, unstaged/untracked work,
saved continuation commits and local task branch tips. A single database
transaction releases the proved legacy owners and terminal pins, increments
workspace generations, disables the source workspaces with an `operator:` reason,
retires task waits and continuations, and clears stale execution assignment.
The `project.retained_holder_recovered` event records the original evidence and
checkpoint refs. Task status, retries and recovery holds remain unchanged.
Files, index and claim markers remain intact. Checkpoints are not restored or
published automatically. A refused apply may leave extra preservation refs.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`global_operator_required` rejects insufficient authority. `proof_required`
requires a preview, and `proof_changed` requires inspecting a new preview.
`retained_holder_unproved` identifies a missing or foreign binding, an unavailable
commit, live/unknown writer evidence, an active job, or ownership reserved to the
modern integration/delegation recovery protocol. These failures release nothing.

## Example step

Use the operator CLI; inspect the returned snapshot before repeating the command
with `--apply --expected-proof <proof>` and identical identities and reason:

```bash
aq project recover-retained-holder --project-id project --task-id task \
  --session-id historical-session --reason "Historical failed publication"
```
